# OSS Security Knowledge Base Update: Eclipse Jetty (`org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-server`)

## Executive Summary

Analysis of 26 public advisories spanning 2006–2026 reveals a deeply studied but historically vulnerability-dense HTTP server component. Recurring vulnerability themes cluster around **HTTP request parsing/smuggling**, **denial of service (resource exhaustion)**, **information disclosure**, and **response injection (XSS)**. The breadth of affected version lines (4.x through 12.x) and the continued discovery of new issues indicate that Jetty's attack surface warrants ongoing vigilance, especially for organizations running older branches.

---

## Grouped Recurring Themes

### 1. HTTP Request Smuggling / Inconsistent Request Handling (Critical–High)

| Advisory | CVE | Fix Version(s) | CVSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| GHSA-6x9x-8qw9-9pp6 | CVE-2017-7658 | 9.2.25, 9.3.24, 9.4.11 | 9.8 Critical |
| GHSA-84q7-p226-4x5w | CVE-2017-7656 | 9.3.24, 9.4.11 | 7.5 High |
| GHSA-vgg8-72f2-qm23 | CVE-2017-7657 | 9.2.25, 9.3.24 | 9.8 Critical |
| GHSA-q4rv-gq96-w7c5 | CVE-2024-13009 | 9.4.57 (unsupported) | 7.2 High (S:C) |

**Pattern:** Jetty has experienced repeated flaws in HTTP request boundary detection and transfer-encoding handling. Three critical/high-severity smuggling CVEs were addressed simultaneously in mid-2018. CVE-2024-13009 (GzipHandler causing request body bleed) demonstrates the theme persists into 2024, and notably was assigned **while the 9.4 branch was unsupported**.

**KB Recommendation:** Flag HTTP smuggling as a **recurring systemic risk** for Jetty. Downstream consumers (reverse proxy architectures) should validate that their Jetty version post-dates the 9.4.11/9.3.24 combined fix and audit GzipHandler configurations against CVE-2024-13009.

---
